questions.moduleTitle: Introduction to Composer 2 and Core Concepts
questions.lessonContent: Composer 2 is trained in two distinct phases: first, continued pretraining to improve the model's knowledge and latent coding ability, followed by large-scale reinforcement learning to improve end-to-end coding performance through stronger reasoning, accurate multi-step execution, and coherence on long-horizon realistic coding problems. The continued pretraining stage aims to improve the language model's base knowledge specifically in the domain of coding and is divided into three phases: bulk compute at 32k token sequence length, followed by a longer-context extension phase to 256k sequence length, and finally a short SFT phase on targeted coding tasks. These phases collectively provide a base model for the subsequent agentic RL training by specializing the model on coding knowledge and capabilities.

These tools form the foundation of the model's ability to interact with software engineering environments. Its prompt includes a system message, the tool call format specification, recent file information, past user messages, and the current task. The most common end result of this process is a set of changes to files in the codebase environment, although there are many other common use cases such as answering questions, writing plans, resolving version control issues, or monitoring long-running jobs.

questions.moduleTitle: Training Methodology: Continued Pretraining and Reinforcement Learning
questions.lessonContent: Composer 2 extends the Kimi K2.5 base model through a continued pretraining stage divided into three distinct phases. The first and most computationally intensive phase uses a 32k token sequence length on a code-dominated data mix. The second phase is a shorter long-context extension that extends the sequence length to 256k tokens. The third and final phase is a brief supervised fine-tuning phase focused on targeted coding tasks. Training was performed using MXFP8 precision on NVIDIA B300s GPUs with the AdamW optimizer.

questions.moduleTitle: Training Methodology: Continued Pretraining and Reinforcement Learning
questions.lessonContent: The Composer 2 training uses Kullback-Leibler divergence for regularization, calculated as KL(q||p) = Ex~q[-log r(x)] where r(x) = p(x)/q(x). While many open-source implementations use the k3 estimator defined as (r - 1) - log r, which is unbiased and reduces variance when p and q are close, the research found that variance increases drastically as p and q diverge. For large KL values, the k3 estimator variance becomes extremely large. Therefore, Composer 2 uses the standard k1 estimator instead, which is simply -log r.

These solutions are assessed through Evaluate Solution Quality using reward signals, and finally the model Update Model Weights based on the computed advantages. This cycle repeats for each problem in the distribution.

While the k3 estimator (defined as (r - 1) - log r) is an unbiased estimator that reduces variance when p and q are close, research shows its variance increases drastically as p and q diverge. For large KL values, the variance of the k3 estimate becomes extremely large, which can destabilize training. The k2 estimator does not suffer from variance blow-up but is biased. Composer 2 chooses k1 over k3 to avoid this variance issue during training.

questions.lessonContent: Composer 2 uses Context Parallelism (CP) as the primary long-context scaling axis for training, requiring less communication than Tensor Parallelism and improving compute efficiency by preserving full hidden dimensions. The implementation includes several key techniques: computing local KV latent vectors then all-gathering across CP ranks before computing KV projections to minimize communication overhead. To address load imbalance during causal attention where later tokens must attend to more tokens, Composer 2 splits the sequence into 2 × CP chunks, with the i-th rank processing chunks i and 2 × CP − 1 − i, resulting in roughly equal work during causal attention. The context parallelism dimension is folded into the FSDP dimension to reduce per-GPU parameter and state memory usage.
